signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-04 ppt-web-core IoT WebSocket reconnect has no cap/backoff)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/iot/hooks/useIotWebSocket.ts:88-95 — the `ws.onclose` handler unconditionally re-arms a reconnect: `reconnectTimer.current = setTimeout(() => { if (!cancelled.current) connect(); }, WS_RECONNECT_MS)` where WS_RECONNECT_MS = 5_000 (line 26). There is NO max-attempt cap and NO exponential backoff — when the IoT WS endpoint is persistently unreachable (Redis not configured, server redeploy, VPN/network outage) the hook reconnects every fixed 5s for the entire lifetime of the mounted telemetry chart, hammering a dead endpoint (and the server auth/upgrade path) indefinitely.

This directly contradicts the repo's own canonical WebSocket client: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:600-620 deliberately added a maxReconnectAttempts cap (default 10) with the comment 'Without this the client would hammer a dead endpoint forever, spamming console + server logs and acting as a small DoS amplifier in dev', plus exponential backoff + jitter (lines 624-628). contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:304-320 further re-arms that capped client on a regained-connectivity signal. The IoT hook implements neither half of that pattern.

Impact (production-reachable): the IoT telemetry page (Epic 14 / FR72) is a real authenticated route. The module docstring itself notes the backend 'returns heartbeat-only frames' or is unreachable 'when Redis is not configured' — i.e. the unreachable case is an expected, documented runtime state, exactly when the uncapped 5s loop fires continuously. Degraded battery/CPU on the client and needless upgrade-handshake load on api-server.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the loop structure and absence of any attempt counter / backoff are confirmed by direct read; what is not runtime-confirmed is how aggressively the server rejects the repeated upgrades.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only, single file): track an attempt counter + cap it (mirror lib/websocket.ts), and compute the delay as `Math.min(WS_RECONNECT_MS * 2 ** attempt, maxDelay) * (0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5)`; stop after N attempts and expose an offline flag. Verifies with `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck && pnpm --filter @ppt/web test` + biome; no backend coupling.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-04 ppt-web-core message send-with-attachments partial failure duplicates the message on retry)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/messaging/hooks/useMessaging.ts:260-273 — performSendWithAttachments() first does `const sendResponse = await api.sendMessage(threadId, { content })` (the message is now persisted server-side with a real id), THEN loops `for (const pending of data.attachments ?? []) await uploadAndLinkAttachment(...)`. uploadAndLinkAttachment (lines ~230-258) does a presigned-PUT to S3 then api.linkMessageAttachment; any of those can throw (network, 5xx, S3 PUT non-2xx — it explicitly `throw new Error("Failed to upload attachment ...")`).

On a mid-loop failure the function rejects, so useSendMessageWithAttachments (lines 284-297) reports `isError` — but the message row ALREADY EXISTS on the server with content and only a partial set of attachments. There is no rollback (no delete of the just-sent message) and no idempotency key on api.sendMessage.

Impact (production-reachable, UC-05.9): the natural UI recovery from a failed send is to retry, which re-invokes performSendWithAttachments → api.sendMessage runs AGAIN and creates a SECOND message (new id) with the same content, then re-uploads all attachments. Result: the recipient sees a duplicate message, and the first (partial) message lingers. Flaky mobile/office networks make attachment-upload failure a routine, not rare, path.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the send-then-upload ordering and the absence of rollback/idempotency are confirmed by direct read; the duplicate only manifests if the user (or an auto-retry) re-runs the mutation after a partial failure, which is the expected recovery.

Fix (frontend-first): either (a) upload+stage attachments to presigned URLs BEFORE calling sendMessage and link them in the same send, or (b) on partial failure delete the just-created message (api.deleteMessage already exists in this file, lines 348-361) before surfacing the error, or (c) pass a client-generated idempotency key so a retry dedupes. Option (b)/(c) is a contained useMessaging.ts change; verifies with `pnpm --filter @ppt/web test` (performSendWithAttachments is already unit-tested) + typecheck + biome.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-04 ppt-web-core action-queue filter returns stale priority counts)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/dashboard/hooks/useActionQueue.ts:86-114 — applyActionQueueFilters() filters `filteredItems` by type/priority/search and returns `{ items: filteredItems, total: filteredItems.length, counts: data.counts }`. It recomputes `total` from the filtered list but passes through the ORIGINAL unfiltered `data.counts` (the per-priority urgent/high/medium/low tallies).

The hook surfaces both: useActionQueue.ts:355-363 builds `stats = { total: query.data.total, ...query.data.counts }`. So after a priority filter (e.g. show only `low`), `stats.total` reflects the filtered count but `stats.urgent/high/medium` still show the full pre-filter tallies — the priority badges disagree with the visible list and with `total`.

Severity LOW / reachability caveat: the action-queue data path is currently DEV-mock-gated (isActionQueueMockEnabled, lines 76-78) — in production and non-mock dev modes the query returns emptyQueue() (line 301-303), so the mismatch is not user-visible on a prod build TODAY. It is still a genuine correctness bug in exported, unit-tested logic (applyActionQueueFilters is explicitly 'Exported for testing') that will ship the moment the real /api/v1/action-queue backend lands and the mock gate is removed.
Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the counts/total divergence is confirmed by direct read of the return object and the stats assembly.

Fix (trivial, frontend-only): recompute counts from filteredItems in applyActionQueueFilters (same reduce already used in generateMockData lines 276-282) instead of forwarding data.counts. One-function edit; verifies with `pnpm --filter @ppt/web test` (the function has existing coverage) + typecheck + biome.
